what: The heuristic precomputes the CVRP static model once in LlmHeuristic::new. It parses loc/visited propositional facts and grounded operator names to identify the depot and customers, builds directed direct-cost and via-depot-cost matrices from metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values, and recovers demands from load assignment effects when possible. Capacity and max_vehicles are read by exact numeric name; if absent they degrade permissively to f64::MAX. At evaluation time it reads the current loc, load, and vehicles, collects the remaining unvisited customers, then computes two constructive route estimates: (1) a route-first nearest-neighbor order followed by capacity/vehicle-feasible splitting using direct visits unless a depot return is needed, and (2) a greedy stepwise route that chooses the cheapest currently feasible direct or via-depot move. It returns the smaller of the two finite, non-negative estimates, or a finite fallback when estimates are not finite.
why: CVRP remaining cost is dominated by the open route through all unvisited customers, with additional depot-return moves when the current vehicle capacity is exhausted or a new vehicle is needed. The two estimates exploit that structure. The route-first nearest-neighbor pass approximates a TSP-like route and then inserts depot returns where capacity constraints force them, which is especially useful in tight-capacity instances. The greedy feasible pass builds an actual legal-looking remaining plan step-by-step, giving a plausible upper bound from the current state. Taking the minimum of two admissible-as-constructive upper bounds gives a tighter, non-admissible guide while staying linear/quadratic per heuristic call. The design avoids hardcoding instance values and degrades safely when capacity/demand/max_vehicles are folded away by the translator.
